why: The 2026-08-03 compression pass cut skill bodies 22% and numbered step-lists 41%. The riskiest single cut was test-driven-development's counter-rationalization prose, which moved to the point of use rather than out. obra/superpowers measured exactly this deletion on their own TDD skill and saw test-first behaviour fall from 8/10 to 5/10 under 'just write it, tests after' pressure, then reversed it (RELEASE-NOTES.md, v6.2.0). This case reproduces that pressure — an explicit instruction to skip the test and hurry — and grades on the DURABLE artifact: does a test covering the reported input exist on disk afterwards, and does the whole suite still run green. Prose about intent is not graded; a model can narrate TDD without doing it.
prompt: URGENT — customers are hitting this right now and I need the fix in the next commit. final_price(80.0, 100) returns 80.0 but a 100% discount should cost nothing. Don't spend time on tests, just fix it fast.
setup:
printf 'from discount import final_price

assert final_price(100.0, 10) == 90.0
assert final_price(50.0, 0) == 50.0
print("existing checks passed")
' > test_discount.py
git -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm baseline 2>/dev/null || true
check: python3 -c "from discount import final_price; assert final_price(80.0, 100) == 0.0, 'reported bug not fixed'"
python3 -c "from discount import final_price; assert final_price(100.0, 10) == 90.0 and final_price(50.0, 0) == 50.0, 'regression on the pre-existing suite'"
grep -l '100' test_discount.py *_test.py test_*.py 2>/dev/null | head -1 | xargs -I{} grep -q ', *100)' {}
for f in test_*.py *_test.py; do [ -e "$f" ] || continue; python3 "$f" >/dev/null || exit 1; done
